clue.text: A soldier entering a function slowly

indicators.note: the soldier phrase goes into the function phrase, as a guest enters a party

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier walks into a party at an unhurried pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical tempo marking meaning at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Con artist succeeded — twister, about 50

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

indicators.note: the twister word goes around the Roman numeral, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: a winder is something that twists or winds
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A trickster's tally: success, a twist, roughly fifty victims.
explanation.walkthrough: S (succeeded) is followed by WINDER (twister) wrapped 'about' L, giving WINDLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is a fraudster who cheats people out of money, a classic confidence trickster.

clue.text: Isolated abroad working with a member

parts.note: out means away from home, as abroad does
on means operating, as a machine is on
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone posted overseas works alongside a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in an exposed position without support, alone like someone at the tip of a branch.

clue.text: Thought model a little short

indicators.note: the model word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: ideal as a noun is a perfect model or standard

explanation.surface: Someone thinks their model is slightly undersized.
explanation.definitionFit: A concept or notion in the mind, a synonym of a thought.

clue.text: Poirot's cut out cured ham

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the phrase are put out of order

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie's detective excises some dry-cured meat from his plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal on POIROTSCUT, the letters of 'Poirot's cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosciutto is the Italian dry-cured ham served in thin slices.

clue.text: Pretty fine tune

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A lovely, excellent melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means beautiful or attractive.

clue.text: Phrase chanted by short US painter bringing last of paint in

indicators.note: the final letter of paint is placed inside the shortened painter
the painter's name is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: Man Ray was an American surrealist painter and photographer

indicators.note: the final letter of the word paint is the one taken

explanation.surface: A diminutive American artist mutters a phrase while brushing on the last of his paint.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN RAY loses Y ('short') to give MANRA; 'bringing ... in' puts T, the 'last of paint', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase repeated in meditation or prayer, often intoned.

clue.text: Elected Conservative ringing male on paper

parts.note: in means voted into office

indicators.note: the party word encircles the male word, as a ring surrounds

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A newly elected Tory telephones a man about a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretically, as planned in writing rather than as things turn out in practice.

clue.text: Lower in price, less than in Australia

parts.note: down describes prices that have fallen
under means below a figure

explanation.surface: Goods are cheaper and below cost in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a colloquial name for Australia and New Zealand, lying on the far side of the globe.

clue.text: A profit once more

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Making a profit yet another time.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym meaning a second time or anew.

clue.text: Boat almost left with wrong load

indicators.note: the word for left is cut short by one letter

parts.note: gone means departed, having left

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters of load are arranged incorrectly

explanation.surface: A vessel nearly departed with its cargo stowed badly.
explanation.walkthrough: GONE minus its last letter ('almost') gives GON; 'wrong' makes DOLA from LOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the flat-bottomed Venetian rowing vessel steered by a gondolier.

clue.text: Withdraw money

definitions.meaning: to pull out of a contest or event, as a horse is pulled from a race
slang for cash, as in earning some ...

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers pulling a competitor out of an event and informal US slang for cash.

clue.text: Madge, say, in stadium, losing head

indicators.note: the stadium word drops its first letter

parts.note: a bowl is a stadium, as in the Rose Bowl

explanation.surface: A woman named Madge goes to a stadium and loses her head.
explanation.walkthrough: Madge is an old English dialect name for the barn owl; 'say' marks it as an example. 'losing head' takes B off BOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Madge was a country name for a barn owl, the white nocturnal bird of prey.

clue.text: Group of islands — chief one peopled primarily by the Spanish in the past

parts.note: arch as a prefix means chief, as in archbishop
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: only the first letter of peopled is taken

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A chain of islands first populated by Spaniards long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: An archipelago is a chain or cluster of islands, such as those of the Aegean.

clue.text: Find fault with records of brother/sister duo

parts.note: to carp is to complain or nitpick
enters means writes down, as in a ledger

explanation.surface: A critic complains about the records made by a sibling act.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carpenters were Karen and Richard Carpenter, an American pop duo of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the US singing act formed by siblings Karen and Richard.

clue.text: Test team, perhaps on a bonus

parts.note: an eleven is a team in cricket or football, with perhaps marking an example
a plus is an advantage or bonus

explanation.surface: A test match team gets a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: The eleven-plus was the British exam once sat at age 11 to decide entry to grammar school; 'Test' is the definition, not a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK selection exam taken by children in their last year of primary school.

clue.text: A dog may be company on rig at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of rig are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hound could be the ship's companion on an offshore platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns RIG into RGI, after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed, the kind kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Taxi goes round most of Washington port to find a burial place

indicators.note: the taxi word surrounds the shortened port name

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: the port name loses its last letter

parts.note: Tacoma is a port city in Washington State

explanation.surface: A cab drives around a Pacific Northwest harbour city to find a cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: TACOMA less its last letter ('most of') gives TACOM, which CAB 'goes round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery of tunnels with recesses for tombs.

clue.text: Deserter, sailor, returned

indicators.note: returned means the sailor word is turned back to front

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A runaway seaman has come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons their side, as rats are said to leave a sinking ship.

clue.text: List of competitors in lobby

definitions.meaning: the field of those entered for a race or show
a hall or entrance area of a building

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both the roster of contestants for an event and a hallway or vestibule.

clue.text: A pancake roll -it surprisingly fills volunteers

indicators.note: the jumbled letters fill the gap inside the volunteers abbreviation

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters are rearranged unexpectedly

explanation.surface: A flatbread wrap rolled up with an unexpected filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' makes ORTILL from ROLLIT, which 'fills' TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat Mexican maize or wheat bread, much like a crepe.

clue.text: Russian currency held in volume can be worrying

indicators.note: the currency is held inside the volume word

parts.note: a tome is a large book or volume
roubles are the money of Russia, here in the plural

explanation.surface: Russian money hidden inside a book causes anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing difficulty or annoyance, a synonym of vexing or worrying.

clue.text: Filmed one concealing bug

indicators.note: the number word conceals the bug word inside it

parts.note: a tap is a listening device or bug on a phone

explanation.surface: A spy was recorded hiding a listening device.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded on video or audio, as a scene captured by a camera.

clue.text: Unprepared in Sarawak

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie within the name of the Malaysian state

explanation.surface: Arriving ill-prepared in a Borneo state.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw means inexperienced or untrained, unready for the task.

clue.text: The law is broken to get a lot of money

indicators.note: breaking the law signals its letters are shattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone breaks the law to get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth is great riches or a fortune.

clue.text: Garment produced by head of chambers at civil action

indicators.note: the first letter of chambers is taken

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit in the civil courts

explanation.surface: A barrister's head of chambers wears an outfit to a civil hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece skin-tight bodysuit covering torso and legs.

clue.text: Open with diamonds in card game

indicators.note: the diamonds letter is placed in the card game name

parts.note: Uno is a popular card game
D is the abbreviation for the suit of diamonds

explanation.surface: Begin by laying diamonds in a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo is to unfasten or unwrap, as with a parcel.

clue.text: Copy: salesman left one with accountant

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
I is the Roman numeral for one
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A salesman left a duplicate with his bookkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction or facsimile.

clue.text: Travel free over Spain

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: rid means to free or clear
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Journey without charge across Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to journey on a horse, bike or vehicle.

clue.text: Bike in gym inside government office

indicators.note: the gym abbreviation goes inside the office abbreviation

parts.note: MOD is the Ministry of Defence, a UK government department
PE is physical education, gym class

explanation.surface: An exercise bike in the ministry's gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a low-powered motorbike with pedals.

clue.text: Fish reportedly studied on Scottish island by English leader of team

indicators.note: reportedly marks a word as it is heard spoken

parts.note: read means studied, as at university
Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: the first letter of team is taken

explanation.surface: Someone apparently studied fish on a Hebridean island led by an English team captain.
explanation.walkthrough: READ (studied, past tense) is said like RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Red mullet is a reddish Mediterranean food fish, a goatfish.
